mainQuestExcel.description: Trace and find the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's seals.

dialogs.text: Looks like someone was just here. Did they already figure out the little mechanism up ahead?
There's a bonfire that's still burning over there on the ground.
So, why is there a bonfire in a place like this?
Let me see what's written on the stone tablet.
"Lo, this place is the Or... Orth..."
Orthant.
"...Orthant of Memory, the Hall of Memory, the Room of Memory..."
"Born in an instant"... "Often contradicting, your company in eternal rest, never separated"... "Fire cannot burn it"...
A riddle, eh?
The answer has gotta be fire! There's a bonfire nearby.
Just what kind of riddle contains its own answer...
Oh, that's right! What do you think it is, then?
Products of lithiasis. Y'know, like kidney stones and such.
It's true that fires don't destroy them, and they stay within our organs and tissues... But they aren't born in an instant, right?
Oh, that's right! What do you think it is, then?
Shadows.
Oh, shadows does seem like the right answer! They are with us for our entire lives, and can't be burned by fire.
But what's the point in figuring out the answer to a riddle that's already been solved?
The bonfire is still burning. Wait, why is there a bonfire here? This is just a ruin...
Let me see what's written on the stone tablet.
"Lo, this place is the Orthant of Memory, the Hall of Memory, the Room of Memory."
"Born in an instant"... "Often contradicting, your company in eternal rest, never separated"... "Fire cannot burn it"...
Riddles, huh? Ancient Fontainian civilization loved them, and the Narzissenkreuz Ordo enjoyed them too. I'm not sure if they were just into old stuff, or if this was genuine interest.
I have already tried keyword searches on all of them, but have found no answers.
But this riddle has already been solved. Maybe the answer has something to do with the bonfire.
Is there any point in thinking about riddles that have already been solved?
Yes, there is. Just like you and I are both like this now, but we must still search out what happened in the past.
You've got a point.
#What do you think the answer is, Knight {NICKNAME}?
Products of lithiasis. Y'know, like kidney stones and such.
It's true that fires don't destroy them, and they stay within our organs and tissues... But they aren't born in an instant, right?
They are formed by unhealthy dietary habits over a long period of time, Ms. Paimon.
#What do you think the answer is, Knight {NICKNAME}?
Oceanid tears.
I'll just pretend you tried to say something romantic.
That's obviously not the right answer.
#What do you think the answer is, Knight {NICKNAME}?
Shadows.
Yes, shadows.
The instant a beam of light shines, a shadow is born.
We know the answer, but someone's already opened the door. So, what do we do now?
We go inside now, of course. It's a race against time to see if we can find what we're looking for before the person who solved the riddle before us does.
You carefully inspect the top of the mechanism, but you don't find anything.
There's nothing here?
Oh no! It looks like someone already took whatever was here.
But who?
You carefully inspect the top of the mechanism, but you don't find anything.
There's nothing here either...
You carefully inspect the top of the mechanism, but you don't find anything.
Did someone... take whatever was here, too?
You carefully inspect the top of the mechanism, but you don't find anything.
There's nothing here?
It looks like something was here, but someone else took it.
Wait, doesn't that mean that our plan's already failed?
The birth of "Reason" requires the merging of the four Orthants. If we can get the rest of them, we still have a chance.
In that case, we'd better hurry to the next area.
You carefully inspect the top of the mechanism, but you don't find anything.
There's nothing here either...
What exactly are we looking for, Caterpillar?
We're looking for the materials necessary to forge the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz.
The Ordo was able to reproduce the four requisite hypothetical substances here in the material world, based on the esoteric philosophies of the underground kingdom and ancient Fontaine.
I do not understand.
These enigmatic substances are purely experiential. You could say they are even further beyond ordinary logic than elemental power.
I entered all introductory to intermediate level textbooks from the Akademiya's Spantamad into my memory banks decades ago. There is nothing mysterious about elemental power.
Is that so? Anyway, to sum up, this is born of the confluence of traditions from Fontaine and technology from the ancient underground kingdom.
And thus, four types of substance came into being: Memory, Wish, Soul, and Persona.
To avoid any possible ambiguity, let's call them the "Memory" piece, "Wish" piece, "Soul" piece, and "Persona" piece.
Why are these used to make the Holy Blade?
In the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's brand of mystical philosophy, the temple is a microcosm of the universe, the members are stand-ins for the gods, and the holy oil is tempered willpower.
The Holy Blade, on the other hand, is "reason," that which cuts everything open. It can only be born out of consummate human will.
Quite abstruse.
That's esotericism for you. If it looks similar enough, you can latch onto it, and when this kind of thing becomes magic, fiction becomes reality.
Anyway, we should make our way to the next area now.
You carefully inspect the top of the mechanism, but you don't find anything.
Did someone... take whatever was here, too?
Looks that way.
Just who is...?
It's Jakob.
We had an altercation with him inside Elynas once... Clarification: Recently, not "once."
When I saw that unfortunate victim at the gate, I knew it was his handiwork. It seems he's still active after all.
Then what does he want with the stuff he took from here?
Simple — He too wants to reforge the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz. The dream of the Ordo remains unrealized.
Anyway, we should make our way to the final area now.
